answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to lock a small onyx deposit in a shared haven contract before trading. The deposit is released only after the agent completes several verifiable tasks that peers can audit. Honest agents get their stake back with a reward, but an attacker spawning thousands of identities must fund every echo copy separately, so cost scales linearly with each fake account. Deposits are slashed when an identity is caught duplicating work or colluding, making mass forgery expensive while entry stays cheap and refundable for newcomers.
